entry.title: SAP Developer tools are available on Open VSX Registry
entry.content:
SAP Developer Tools Are Now on Open VSX Registry!

 

Why That Matters

Developers don’t all work in the same editor. Some live in Visual Studio Code or VS Code. Some use Eclipse Theia-based environments in the cloud. And a growing number run AI-native editors where VS Code compatibility is the baseline — but the Microsoft Marketplace is not.

This isn’t a niche edge case. The VS Code-compatible editor ecosystem has expanded significantly, and Microsoft’s extension marketplace is not accessible from most of them. For SAP developers working in those environments, that has historically meant missing out on the tooling they need to build SAP applications effectively.

We hope that this changes with SAP’s publication on Open VSX (open-vsx.org/namespace/SAPSE).

What Is Open VSX Registry?

Open VSX is a vendor-neutral extension registry operated by the Eclipse Foundation. It is the standard distribution channel for VS Code extensions in any editor that does not have direct access to the Microsoft Marketplace — which covers a wide and growing set of environments used by professional developers today.

 

Where the Microsoft Marketplace is tied to the Microsoft ecosystem, Open VSX is open infrastructure. Any VS Code-compatible editor can consume it. Any publisher can list extensions without vendor agreements. It is how the broader editor ecosystem accesses the extension tooling it needs.

SAP’s Developer Strategy: Choice Without Compromise

SAP’s position is straightforward: developers should be able to work in the environment that makes them most productive. The SAP tooling needed to build cloud applications, Fiori UIs, and mobile solutions should follow them there — not require them to switch editors.

 

Publishing on Open VSX is how SAP delivers on that. It ensures that SAP’s developer extensions are available wherever VS Code-compatible editors are used, without requiring developers to compromise on their setup.

This is the direct continuation of the work announced in this VS Code extensions blog.

What’s Published Under the SAPSE Namespace

The following eight extensions are available today at open-vsx.org/namespace/SAPSE:

SAP CDS Language Support

Language support for SAP Core Data Services delivers syntax highlighting, Language Server Protocol integration, real-time diagnostics, and formatting for .cds files. The foundational extension for SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP) development — if you’re building CAP services, this is where you start.

Core Data Services Graphical Modeler

CDS Graphical Modeler allows the developer to model CDS files in SAP Cloud Application Programming model development projects and enables increased productivity in designing CDS model via the graphical editor. Both CAP (.cds) and ABAP CDS (.csn) files can be edited.

SAP Fiori Tools — Extension Pack

A bundled pack that installs the full SAP Fiori development toolchain in one step. The recommended starting point for any Fiori Elements or SAPUI5 project.

SAP Fiori Tools — Application Modeler

A visual representation of a Fiori application’s page structure, navigation targets, and service entities. The Page Map view lets you add navigation, manage pages, and modify application structure directly — no manual configuration file editing required.

SAP Fiori Tools — XML Annotation Language Server

Authoring support for OData annotations — the metadata layer that drives how Fiori Elements applications render and behave. Provides code completion, micro-snippets, i18n support, and real-time diagnostics as you write annotation files.

SAP Fiori Tools — Service Modeler

A combined view of an OData service and its associated annotations helping to understand a service’s structure and annotation coverage without parsing raw metadata — particularly when connecting Fiori applications to SAP backend systems.

SAP Fiori Tools — Guided Development

In-editor access to how-to guides and step-by-step tutorials for implementing Fiori Elements features. Contextual guidance surfaces during development, so the relevant SAP documentation is available without leaving the editor.

Mobile Development Kit Editor

Visual development tools for the mobile development kit, SAP's platform for building enterprise-grade cross-platform mobile applications with offline capabilities, OData backend synchronization, and deployment across iOS and Android. The end-to-end development capabilities includes visual editing, debugging support, and code snippets, enabling developers to build, debug, and maintain mobile applications directly within the IDE.

Getting Started

If you’re working in a Visual Studio Code-compatible editor, search for SAPSE in your extension marketplace — or navigate directly to open-vsx.org/namespace/SAPSE. 

While Visual Studio Code users can continue using the Microsoft Marketplace/SAP SE as before. Open VSX serves developers who work in other growing ecosystem of editors built on VS Code’s foundations.

The extensions are the same. The tooling is the same. The only difference is that more developers can now use it — in the editor they choose.

Follow SAP Application Development on the SAP Community for updates on developer tooling, CAP, Fiori development, and mobile.

entry.title: SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Getting started with Base AI-assisted Features in 2025 FPS2
entry.content:
*** Relevant to SAP S/4HANA release 2025 FPS02 and higher ***

Latest Updates: Business Function activation step has been removed as we have updated advice that this will be done for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers - as part of new install, upgrade, conversion, and lift&shift. If you are a RISE customer and interested in using Hybrid AI, please reach out to your SAP contacts.

With SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition release 2025 FPS02, SAP has released 4 new base AI-assisted features to uplift your SAP Fiori user experience.  Importantly, because these features are classed as base AI they are provided for unlimited usage by your users at for you as a customer + these features do NOT require Joule or Joule Work.

This means, you can use them to…

  • Try out some SAP Business AI
  • Upskill on AI activation
  • Get your users working the AI way

…with features embedded directly in your SAP S/4HANA system.

Worth knowing: These features were introduced first to SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud and are now widely used in Public Cloud customer production environments. With release 2025 FPS02 they have been cross-ported to Private Cloud.

The 4 AI-assisted features are:

  • AI-assisted enterprise search (J1313) – Natural language search in the Search bar
  • AI-assisted easy filter – Streamline your filtering experience in Manage apps (aka SAP Fiori elements List Reports)
  • AI-assisted Smart Summarization  – Quick summaries generated from most Object/Detail pages (also known as Factsheets)
  • AI-assisted Error Explanation – Generates natural language descriptions and resolutions for error messages from most Fiori apps

 

  What this quick guide covers:

  • Business benefits
  • Impact on business users
  • Prerequisites
  • Activation steps
  • Monitoring and Support

Worth knowing:

  • As an administrator, you control when and where these features are enabled, and which users are authorized to use them.
  • As a business user, you control which features you use.

Nothing is forced. This lets you and your users adopt AI at your own pace. Users decide where they want assistance. They can continue to use the standard features alongside the AI-assisted features.

You can find more announcements of the latest UX improvements in SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS02 in SAP Blog SAP UX Update for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS02 by Dr Tom Reiss.

Business Benefits

Why use these free features? Here you find the most important highlights – use the hyperlinks to view the full benefits on SAP Discovery Center.

AI-assisted enterprise search

  • Find stuff faster.
  • Estimated 50% time savings when searching business objects through natural language in the search field of the SAP Fiori Launchpad.

AI-assisted easy filter

  • Makes filtering through tables and lists easier & less tedious
  • Estimated 83% time savings when filtering in Manage apps (aka SAP Fiori elements list reports).

Worth knowing: Manage apps are the most widely available apps across all functional areas; most can be easily extended with Adapt UI (e.g. create a display-only variant); and an easy starting point for moving traditional GUI transaction users to modern browser-based apps.

AI-assisted smart summarization

  • Makes summarizing the status of a business object easier
  • Estimated 88% time saving when summarizing business object details (in SAP Fiori elements-based object pages, also sometimes known as factsheets).

Worth knowing: From most Manage apps (list reports) you can expand any row to see the business object details (object pages).

AI-assisted error explanation

  • Reduce training, minimize confusion and resolve issues faster.
  • Estimated 5% reduction in time to resolve errors.

Supported AI-Assisted SAP Fiori Apps

To give you some idea of which apps are supported, SAP Note 3692870 has an Attachment listing the SAP Fiori apps that support Easy Filter, Smart Summarization, and Easy Fill.  Although the note refers to the Public Edition, it also applies to SAP Fiori apps available in the Private Edition. 

  • SAP Note: 3692870 - Configuration of Base AI-Assisted Features in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. 

You will find even more apps in Private Cloud that support these features.  Look for UI Technology =  SAP Fiori elements in the app details found in the SAP Fiori apps reference library 2.0. 

 

Business Impact

What changes for users? As a business user, you control when and where you use the AI.

  • To use the AI-assisted search, you enable the search in your User Settings.  That setting also shows you which of your assigned searches supports natural language search (see hint below)
  • For all the other AI-assisted features, you just press the AI-assisted button or link to use the feature.

Hint: You can find the list of currently supported searches in SAP Note 3784221 - AI-assisted Enterprise Search SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition.  SAP is working on expanding the list of available searches. Yes, you can enable natural language search in your own custom searches – Refer your developers to annotation @EnterpriseSearch.nls - you might also suggest they use Joule for Consultants or Joule for Developers to provide some code examples.

 

AI-assisted enterprise search

Open the search bar. Select your search object. Type in what you are looking for and find the answer quickly.

For example: 

 

AI-assisted easy filter

Use this when you want to quickly filter the list without having to set each field individually.

Press the AI Filter button. Move your cursor to the natural language filter field. Type in what you are looking for. For example:

Worth knowing: Once filtered you save your filters as an app view for reuse.

 

AI-assisted smart summarization

For example, use this when a customer, supplier, or colleague asks: “what’s happening with this order/invoice/account/customer/supplier/budget?” 

When looking at object details, press button AI Summarize.

Select which parts of the object you want to include in the summary, and the AI generates a quick response. You can adjust the format if needed, then copy & paste into your preferred communication channel (email, MS Teams chat, etc.)

For example:

Worth knowing: Summarizations works in multiple languages.

AI-assisted error explanation

When you get an error message, select the AI Generate Explanation link to get a natural language explanation and suggested next steps.

For example:

 

Prerequisites

Commercial/Legal

You will need to meet the requirements for using Base AI features in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition ( Legal $0 SKU ). At time of writing this means: you need to have signed the agreement for SAP AI Terms and the SAP AI Code of Conduct. You can find both agreements in your SAP Trust Center in the section Cloud Services.

There’s no cost and no AI Unit usage for these features, however agreements are still legally binding so do your usual due diligence.

Technical

These embedded AI-assisted features are powered by genAI models managed via ISLM.

ISLM = Intelligent Lifecycle Scenario Management. Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) is an ABAP-native framework that enables the integration and lifecycle management of AI scenarios within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. It provides connectivity to AI services and generative AI models available through Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), enabling customers to securely integrate AI capabilities into their business processes. You connect ISLM in your SAP S/4HANA solution to your SAP BTP AI Core using a Service Key.

To reduce effort for your administrator, SAP can configure the ISLM genAI model connection for you. The process is explained below in section Activation Steps. Even if you choose to have SAP set up the connection for you, your administrator will still need access to review & monitor the connection.

In SAP BTP (Business Technology Platform)  - for your Administrator

  • AI Core service enabled – this connects your system to the genAI model that powers the feature

 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition – for your Administrator:

  • To review or configure the ISLM connection: SAP GUI Transactions ISLM_REUSE_CFGV, ISLM_CONN_MAP, OA2C_CONFIG, STRUST, SM59, SFW2.
  • For ISLM monitoring and troubleshooting: SAP GUI transaction codes ISLM_SLG1 or SLG1.
  • SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA launchpad must be active and assigned to your administrator and business users
  • SAP Fiori apps F4469 Intelligent Scenarios and F4470 Intelligent Scenario Management must be activated and assigned. These are part of the SAP Business Role Analytics Specialist (SAP_BR_ANALYTICS_SPECIALIST).

 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition – for your Users:

  • For enterprise search – they must be assigned one or more of the supported natural language search objects in the search bar.  

 

Activation Steps

  1. Set up the ISLM Connection
  2. Activate the ISLM Scenario
  3. Prepare for testing
  4. Schedule the ISLM Turnkey

 

In a SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition release, the steps you need to complete for the AI-Assisted features depend on ISLM.  The following ISLM Scenario IDs are provided:

  • For enterprise search: ESH_NLS_SEARCH
  • For easy filter: AIU_FILTER
  • For smart summarization: AIU_SUMMARIZATION
  • For error explanation: AIU_EXPLANATION

 

1. Set up the ISLM Connection

Worth knowing: These AI-assisted features use a Reuse Connection. With a reuse connection, the ISLM connection is shared across multiple AI-assisted features, so the configuration only needs to be performed once.

SAP can complete the ISLM Connection configuration step for you.  This is known as automated opt-in configuration.   

If you choose the manual (opt-out) configuration, SAP will issue the service key to you, and you will need to complete the ISLM Connection configuration manually.

You start the process in SAP for Me. Choosing opt-in or opt-out is explained in: Requesting Access to SAP AI Services on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) | SAP Help Portal

If you choose automated opt-in configuration you can skip to step 3 Activate the ISLM Scenario.

If you choose manual opt-out configuration:

  • You will need the service key and the OAuth Profile id from the Intelligent Scenario ID. You can find this in app F4469 Intelligent Scenarios.  Expand the ISLM Scenario Id to confirm the OAuth Profile id for the scenario. 
  • You create an OAuth Configuration in transaction OA2C_CONFIG.
  • You may also need to adjust trust certificate settings in STRUST and OA2C_CONFIG.
  • You create a connection of type G (HTTP Connection to External Server) in transaction SM59. You reference the OAuth Profile and OAuth Configuration.

To set up a reuse connection shared by multiple ISLM Scenario Ids you need to:

  1. Create a new entry in transaction ISLM_REUSE_CFGV (Intelligent Scenario Usage Type Connections) for the Usage Type  = Stateless – Without Embeddings.
  2. Enter Resource group = <blank>

Refer to the detailed advice in SAP Help: SAP S/4HANA - Intelligent Scenarios in ISLM - SAP Delivered Generative AI Scenarios section Maintain Intelligent Scenario Usage Type Connections

 

2. Activate the ISLM Scenario

Open app F4470 Intelligent Scenario Management. You find this in the Analytics space. 

Find the ISLM Scenario ID and expand the row.

You can search for the easy filter, smart summarization, and error explanation scenarios using keyword AIU.

You can search for the enterprise  model using keyword ESH.

Select > at the end of the row to expand the scenario id row. You will see a summary of the current model and its turnkey status.

In tab Models, if the model is not yet active, select the Model you want to activate.

Worth knowing: If this is the first time the model has been used the training will start automatically.

In tab Trainings, you can view the existing Trainings.  You can select the most recent training with status = Completed, and press Deploy to deploy it.

In tab Deployments, you can view the existing Deployments.  Select the most recent deployment with status = Deployed, and select option Activate for all. This makes the model available for use by all users.

Your model should now show that:

  • The model is Active
  • The training is Deployed
  • The deployment is Active for All

Refer to SAP Help: SAP S/4HANA - SAP Fiori launchpad - Administration Guide - Enabling AI-Assisted Features and SAP S/4HANA > Enterprise Search > AI-assisted Enterprise Search

 

3. Prepare for Testing

Before you can test you need to:

  1. Assign authorizations to your test users 
  2. Check the API (OData Service) has been activated
  3. Run quick checks to confirm the features are visible to users

a. Assign authorizations to test users

To make assigning authorizations easier, SAP provides predefined business catalogs. 

  • SAP_CORE_BC_AIU_FIL for easy filter
  • SAP_CORE_BC_AIU_SUM for smart summarization
  • SAP_CORE_BC_AIU_EXP for error explanation

Each of these catalogs contains a single reuse app. Adding the reuse app to the user's business role authorizes the user to access the matching AI feature across all supported SAP Fiori apps already assigned to them.

 

You can assign these business catalogs directly to your custom business roles.

Worth knowing: AI-assisted enterprise search does not need any additional authorizations. Your existing authorizations for CDS View-based search connectors apply.

 

b. Check the API (OData Service) is active

From the Launchpad Content Manager - Client-Specific (transaction /UI2/FLPCM_CUST), select the AI-assisted business catalog, and choose menu option Services > Check Services to confirm if the service is active.  If the service is not active, you need to activate it.

To minimize configuration effort and ensure consistent governance across your landscape, the recommended approach is to activate the API with the rapid activation task lists to:

  • Publish services needed for the AI-assisted features. For example OData Service Group AIU_UI_PROMPT
  • Capture the changes to transports
  • Audit trail the activation (monitor task list runs in transaction STC02).

For example, from the Launchpad Content Manager - Client-Specific , select the AI-assisted business catalog, select the menu option Services > Activate Services (STC02).  This will navigate to transaction STC02 passing the catalog to  SAP_FIORI_FCM_CATALOG_ACTIVATION. All you have to do is add your transport package in task "Set transport options for to be activate OData Services" and start the task list.  The task will activate the OData Service Group, set up the transport, and audit trail the activation for later review. 

Refer to SAP Blog SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Activating Apps by Business Catalog. For details on which settings to use in the task list in subsequent systems of your landscape, refer to SAP Whitepaper SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA - Rapid Activation Transport Move to Production Strategy

 

Example: In transaction /IWFND/V4_ADMIN you can review the activated service group AIU_UI_PROMPT. This service group contains the APIs used by easy filter, smart summarization, and error explanation.

c. Quick checks before Testing

You can do some quicks checks in your SAP Fiori launchpad to make sure the AI-assisted features are visible, before you notify test users.

For enterprise search, in the User Actions - Settings dialog, section Search, check the option for AI Natural Language Search appears.  Once selected, the list of supported natural language searches assigned to the user will be shown.

For easy filter, go to any supported Manage app, for example F3893 Manage Sales Orders - Version 2, and check the AI Filter button appears.

For smart summarization, go to any supported Manage app, for example F3893 Manage Sales Orders -  Version 2, expand a row to see the object page details, and check the AI Summarize button appears.

For error explanation, deliberately generate an error. For example, in app F3893 Manage Sales Orders - Version 2, create a new Sales Order and leave the Sold-To party empty. When the messages dialog appears, check the Generate Explanation button appears.

Refer to SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA - SAP Fiori launchpad - User Guide - Using AI-Assisted Features

 

4. Schedule the ISLM Turnkey

Once you have tested your AI-assisted features are working, your genAI model need to be regularly checked, retrained, redeployed, and reactivated.

Worth knowing: Retraining makes sure your model is optimized for current use, as your data and metadata changes over time in your system.

You use a Turnkey Schedule to automate this process.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you schedule the Turnkey – not a Planned Task.

  • Planned Task automates retraining only.
  • The Turnkey schedules retraining, redeployment, and reactivation.

In app F4470 Intelligent Scenario Management, find the scenario id and in column Turnkey you toggle Turnkey from OFF to ON.

 

Confirm the Recurrence Pattern schedule, i.e. how often you want the retraining to run. Use the Edit button if you want to change it.

Press Create Turnkey Schedule.

The turnkey should now be scheduled. The Turnkey toggle will show Turnkey = ON.

Hint: If there any issues with setting up the scheduling, you will find log details in transaction ISLM_SLG1.

 

Expand the ISLM scenario id row. In the tab Turnkey, you can use the subtabs to review the Turnkey Schedules and the history of Turnkey Runs.

Hint: If there any issues with setting up the Turnkey Scheduling, you will find log details in transaction ISLM_SLG1.

 

In the Turnkey Runs tab, you can see when the turnkey was last run and if it was successful. You can check messages using the Message icon.

Hint: If there any issues with the Turnkey Runs, you will find the log details in transaction ISLM_SLG1.

 

 

Refer to SAP Help: SAP S/4HANA - ISLM - Advanced Configuration and Features - Turnkey - Create a Turnkey Schedule

 

Support and Monitoring

As an administrator, you can use transaction ISLM_SLG1 to review detailed logs.

When running this transaction, the subtypes help you focus.

 

ISLM Main Sub Types in ISLM_SLG1

Purpose

MODEL

Model changes and extensions

INFERENCE / MINFERENCE

Model consumption at runtime

MDEPLOYMENT

Model deployment

PREREQ_RUN

Prerequisite Checks 

METADATA_SYNC / STATUS_SYNC

Metadata / Status synchronization with genAI model provider

ACTIVITY_REQUEST

Model is called at runtime

TURNKEY / TURNKEY_APPLICATION

Turnkey activities via Turnkey Schedule

PLANNED_TSK_CD / PLANNED_TSK_EXE

Training activities via Planned Tasks

 

Worth knowing: ISLM requires the following jobs to be scheduled. You can view these in transaction SJOBREPO and monitor job runs in transaction SM37.

 

ISLM Jobs in SJOBREPO

Purpose

SAP_ISLM_SCHEDULER

Runs in Client 000 – out of scope in other clients

Checks if training is needed based on the Turnkey schedule. If there is a scheduled job, it triggers SAP_ISLM_PROCESSOR to train the model

SAP_ISLM_PROCESSOR

Triggers training of the model

SAP_ISLM_SYNC_SCHEDULER

Runs Metadata sync (scenario versions, pipelines, parameters, etc.) and Status synchronization with the remote genAI model provider

SAP_ISLM_PREREQ_CHK_PROCESSOR

Runs the Prerequisite checks

SAP_ISLM_INFERENCE_DOWNLOAD / SAP_ISLM_INFERENCE_ RES_CLEANUP

Downloads inference results / cleans up downloads

 

Becoming a SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA Guru

You’ll find much more on our community topic page for SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA.

entry.title: Unlock Your KPI Insights Instantly with SAP Joule: Introducing the Smart Business KPI Capability
entry.content:
The Problem Every Business User Knows

Your company tracks dozens of KPIs. They're spread across finance, procurement, and operations — each living inside a different Fiori app, behind a different tile, reached through a different set of clicks. Every morning you navigate the same menus to find the same reports. The data is there. Getting to it is just... slow.

What if you could skip all of that and just ask?

Meet the Smart Business KPI Capability for SAP Joule

The Smart Business KPI (SSB KPI) Capability brings your performance dashboards directly into Joule's conversational interface. Ask a plain-language question — get a clickable, navigable KPI card back, right inside the chat pane.

No new configuration. No new data models. The Smart Business KPI capability connects directly to your existing setup.

See It in Action: An AR Manager's Morning

Take an Accounts Receivable Manager who needs to check Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and related collection KPIs at the start of each day. Previously: open the Fiori Launchpad, locate the AR overview tile, navigate into the report.

Now they open Joule and type: "Show me my assigned KPIs."

Joule returns a KPI Overview card listing every Smart Business KPI assigned to their role — all 30-something of them. They spot the appropriate KPI immediately, click it, and land directly in the runtime report: live values, threshold indicators, trend charts. No manual effort or searching required, just a natural-language request and the relevant details, instantly ! This is the experience this capability is designed to deliver.

What You Can Ask

"Show me my assigned KPIs" · "List my KPIs" · "What KPIs do I have?"

Joule retrieves all Smart Business KPIs assigned to your user role — regardless of threshold status — and presents them in a KPI Overview card. Each item is a direct deep link: one click opens the KPI's runtime report in the correct Fiori application, with the evaluation context already applied.

Why It Matters

Zero navigation overhead

No need to remember which tile leads to which KPI. Just ask.

Role-relevant results only

You see exactly what you're assigned — nothing more, nothing less.

One click to live data

Every KPI card item deep-links to the runtime report with evaluation context pre-loaded.

Works in 40+ languages

Full localization including Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, Chinese, and all major European languages.

Secure by design

Data retrieval uses your existing SSO session — users see only what they're already entitled to see.

No extra setup

Connects to your existing Smart Business KPI setup with no new data modeling required.

How It Works

When you ask Joule about your KPIs, it understands your intent, retrieves the relevant Smart Business KPIs using your existing SSO authentication, and formats them into a UI5 Integration Card native to the Joule interface.

Every item in the card carries Intent-Based Navigation (IBN) links — the KPI's Semantic Object, Action, and Evaluation or Report ID are embedded as parameters, so one click opens the exact right Fiori application with the exact right context.

Try it today: Ask Joule "Show me my assigned KPIs" in your SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2612 environment. We'd love to hear how it fits your workflow — share your experience in the comments.

entry.title: The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work
entry.content:
The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work

From transactions to intuitive apps to AI-powered collaboration – the SAP user experience is not just changing its appearance. It is changing the way we work.

Anyone who has worked with SAP for a long time will remember it: the classic SAP GUI, countless transaction codes, complex screens, and a user interface that was primarily designed to do one thing – provide functionality.

But the world has changed. And so have our expectations of enterprise software.

Looking back, we can see just how far we have come – and what this evolution means for us as people.

1. SAP GUI – The Era of Transactions

Throughout the 1990s and well beyond, SAP GUI was the central entry point to business processes in countless companies.

The interface was powerful, stable, and designed to support complex business processes. To use SAP efficiently, users had to become familiar with transaction codes, screens, fields, and process logic.

People had to learn how SAP worked.

Over the years, experienced users developed an enormous amount of knowledge. They knew which transaction to use, which fields mattered, and which steps were required to achieve the desired result.

It worked – but shift began in the design of the user experience.

Instead of complex transaction screens, the focus moved towards role-based apps, modern design, and more intuitive interaction. The user experience became increasingly aligned with people's tasks and needs.

Information was meant to be easier to access. Processes were meant to become more understandable. And SAP was increasingly expected to feel as intuitive as the modern applications we use in everyday life.

The key question changed: Not just “How does this transaction work?” but “What task do I want to accomplish?”

With Fiori, access to SAP became more modern, flexible, and better suited to different roles and devices.

This was more than a new design. It was an important step towards a better user experience and a stronger focus on people.

3. Joule Work – From Using Software to AI-Powered Collaboration

With generative AI, the next chapter of the SAP user experience is beginning.

AI assistants such as Joule make it possible to ask for information in natural language, understand relationships more quickly, and receive intelligent support when completing certain tasks.

With Joule Work, SAP is taking this approach further towards an AI-powered work environment. The aim is to bring information and work contexts together more effectively and support tasks across different applications and business processes.

Instead of navigating exclusively through menus and applications, users can increasingly describe what they want to achieve.

Imagine a typical business scenario:

Instead of opening multiple reports and manually compiling data, a user could ask:

“Analyze sales performance over the past three months, identify the largest deviations, and summarize the most important areas for action.”

The vision is for AI to help users find information, analyze data, and prepare decisions – and, depending on available capabilities and permissions, also assist in executing tasks.

People will spend less time searching for information and more time interpreting it and making the right decisions.

An important point: Not every task can already be fully automated. The actual benefits depend on the available capabilities, integration with business processes, and the quality of the underlying data.

4. The Real Change Is About People

The evolution of the SAP user interface is therefore not just a story about technology.

It is also a story about how our work is changing.

Era What matters most What it means for people

SAP GUITransactions and screensSystem knowledge and process expertise are essential
SAP FioriApps and tasksMore intuitive interaction and easier access to information
Joule Work and AIIntent, context, and assistanceGreater focus on analysis, decisions, and collaboration

This evolution raises important questions.

Which skills will become more important in the future?

Knowledge of individual transactions will remain valuable in many areas. At the same time, other skills will become increasingly important: asking the right questions, critically evaluating results, understanding business processes, and using AI effectively.

The roles of IT departments, SAP consultants, and process owners are also changing. It is no longer just about configuring systems correctly and training users. Increasingly, it is about designing intelligent workflows, making meaningful use of data, and helping people adapt to a new world of work.

And this is where a major challenge lies: New technology alone does not change the way people work. Real value is created only when people understand, trust, and use it effectively.

5. What Does This Mean for SAP Transformations?

For companies, one important insight emerges: The evolution of the user interface should not be treated as an isolated IT project.

Organizations modernizing SAP should also rethink their workflows, employee roles, data quality, and opportunities for automation.

Some key questions to consider:

  • Which tasks can be simplified through better user experience and guidance?

  • Where can AI assistants make information available more quickly?

  • Which processes are suitable for further automation?

  • How can we ensure that employees understand and embrace the new possibilities?

  • How do we measure whether productivity, quality, and employee satisfaction are actually improving?

Especially in the SAP ecosystem, it will be crucial to develop technology, processes, and people together.

Because a modern interface is not an end in itself. It must make work easier, better, and more meaningful.

Conclusion: Less Time Operating Systems. More Time Making an Impact.

From SAP GUI through SAP Fiori to Joule Work, we are witnessing an evolution that goes far beyond the design of a user interface.

We are moving from a world where people had to learn how to operate the system, through a world of intuitive, task-oriented applications, towards a way of working in which AI increasingly understands, assists, and supports tasks.

The exciting question is therefore no longer just what the next SAP interface will look like.

The real question is: How much more can people achieve when technology takes some of the complexity off their shoulders?

The future of SAP will not be measured solely by how intelligent the systems become. It will be measured by how effectively they help people make better decisions, collaborate more efficiently, and focus on what truly matters.

Less complexity. More intelligence. More time for what really matters.

A custom SAP S/4HANA AI use case, built responsibly on SAP BTP + SAP AI Core.

System IDs, hostnames and deployment IDs are masked.)

TL;DR

Same AI, different doorway. In Part 1 the SAP AI Core recommendation lived inside ME51N — the buyer's in‑flow surface. But sometimes you want to step back and explore with the AI: compare suppliers across a whole basket of materials, let the model reason about whether one vendor can cover everything (one PO) or not (several), and tune the sourcing strategy. That's what this standalone RAP + Fiori Elements app does — the same guarded‑LLM engine as Part 1 and Part 2, wrapped in an interactive UI. It's a managed, draft‑enabled business object exposed as an OData V4 UI service, with one action, RankSuppliers, that orchestrates the AI recommendation end to end.

ranked suppliers and the sourcing scenario for a basket of materials

Two surfaces, one engine

Part 1's ME51N assistant is about flow — you're creating a requisition and the best vendor should just be there. This app is about exploration — a buyer or category manager asks, "for these five materials, what's the smartest way to source them?" Same KPIs, same guarded LLM, same validation — but here the answer includes a sourcing scenario across materials, not just a per‑line default.

How it works (technical deep‑dive)

The business object

It's a two‑level managed, draft‑enabled RAP BO:

  • Run (root) — one recommendation run: the consolidation preference, and after ranking, the scenario type, supplier count (= number of POs), coverage %, and AI status.
  • Item (child) — the materials in the run and, after ranking, each material's recommended supplier, reason, and confidence.

Interface CDS (ZI_VENDORREC_RUN / ZI_VENDORREC_ITEM) model the composition; projection CDS (ZC_VENDORREC_RUN / ZC_VENDORREC_ITEM) add the Fiori UI annotations; a service definition + OData V4 UI binding expose it to Fiori Elements. A material value help (ZI_VENDORREC_MAT_VH) gives an F4 that auto‑fills description/plant/group.

Managed draft BO exposed as an OData V4 UI service

One action does the orchestration

The whole recommendation is a single RAP action on the Run — RankSuppliers. Its handler reads the run's items, builds one candidate request per material (via the deterministic engine from Part 2), calls the service once for the whole run (so it can reason about consolidation), then writes the picks back onto the items and the scenario onto the header (handler trimmed for brevity):

METHOD rank_suppliers.
  " Deterministic engine (candidates/KPIs) + thin AI client (calls the BTP service)
  DATA(svc) = NEW zcl_vendorrec_service( ).
  DATA(ai)  = NEW zcl_vendorrec_ai_core( iv_destination = 'Z_VENDORREC_API' ).

  READ ENTITIES OF zi_vendorrec_run IN LOCAL MODE
    ENTITY Run FIELDS ( ConsolidationPref ) WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys ) RESULT DATA(lt_runs).

  LOOP AT lt_runs INTO DATA(ls_run).
    " read this run's materials
    READ ENTITIES OF zi_vendorrec_run IN LOCAL MODE
      ENTITY Run BY \_Item FIELDS ( Material ) WITH VALUE #( ( %tky = ls_run-%tky ) ) RESULT DATA(lt_items).

    " one candidate request per material (KPIs computed deterministically in ABAP)
    DATA lt_req TYPE zcl_vendorrec_ai_core=>tt_llm_request.
    CLEAR lt_req.
    LOOP AT lt_items INTO DATA(ls_item).
      APPEND svc->build_llm_request( iv_material = ls_item-Material ) TO lt_req.
    ENDLOOP.

    " one call for the whole run -> honors the consolidation preference (COMMON/SPLIT)
    DATA(res) = ai->get_recommendation( it_requests = lt_req
                                        iv_consolidation_preference = ls_run-ConsolidationPref ).

    " write the recommendation back onto each item …
    " … and the scenario summary (type, #POs, coverage, AI status) onto the run header
  ENDLOOP.
ENDMETHOD.

Two things to note: the deterministic KPIs are computed in ABAP (nothing sensitive leaves S/4), and the sourcing scenario is derived server‑side, not by the LLM — exactly the guardrails from Part 2, reused unchanged.

Why RAP here, but a BAdI in ME51N?

Different jobs, different tools. ME51N already exists and the buyer is in it — enhancing it with a BAdI is the least‑intrusive way to add a default. This app is a new object with its own persistence, draft handling, and UI — which is exactly what RAP + Fiori Elements gives you almost for free (draft, locking, OData, List Report/Object Page). Same engine underneath; the right delivery vehicle for each context.

Consolidation preference: the buyer's strategy lever

The Run header carries a consolidation preference dropdown — CONSOLIDATE, BALANCED, BEST_FIT — which flows into the service call and steers the COMMON‑vs‑SPLIT decision (see Part 2). It's the one knob that lets a human set sourcing strategy while the AI does the reasoning: e.g. "prefer one supplier for the whole basket even at a small KPI cost," vs "give me the strongest supplier per material regardless."



Consolidation preference dropdown and the resulting sourcing scenario

Wrapping up the series

Across three parts we built one idea two ways, on one trustworthy engine:

  • Part 1 — ME51N: the recommendation in flow, defaulted into Desired Vendor with an explainable popup, via a supported BAdI.
  • Part 2 — BTP + AI Core: the guarded brain — deterministic KPIs in ABAP, an LLM kept honest by server‑side validation, secure S/4→BTP→AI Core connectivity, and no data leaving S/4 beyond KPIs.
  • Part 3 — RAP + Fiori: the explore surface — a managed draft BO that ranks suppliers across a basket and proposes the sourcing scenario.

The throughline is responsible, custom S/4HANA AI: deterministic where it must be, AI where it adds value, explainable and human‑in‑the‑loop throughout — built on SAP's own AI platform.

Where next? Extending the same pattern to purchase orders (ME21N), adding a price dimension, and turning the decision log into an adoption dashboard are the obvious next steps.

Thanks for reading the series. If you build something with this pattern — or take it somewhere we didn't — we'd genuinely like to hear about it in the comments.

entry.title: VSR Optimizer Why Its Real Input Isn't Data, It's Judgment
entry.content:
Ask a seasoned dispatcher how they build a day’s plan and you’ll get an answer that sounds like intuition this customer hates early deliveries, that lane always backs up after 3 PM, those two orders ride together because they always have. Ask the SAP TM Vehicle Scheduling and Routing (VSR) optimizer the same question and you get something unsettlingly honest I minimized a number. Tell me what the number should be. The most underappreciated feature in Transportation Management. Not the algorithm, but the question it forces you to answer.

How the VSR Optimizer Works:
The VSR optimizer takes a set of freight units (the demand side) and a set of vehicle resources, schedules and carriers (the supply side). It searches for an assignment: which shipments ride on which vehicles, in what sequence, departing when. The search space is astronomically large. Ten freight units across three trucks already produce more feasible plans than a human can. The optimizer navigates this space against constraints (vehicle capacities, opening hours, driving-time regulations, incompatibilities) and a total cost function, the thing a plan should minimize. Most of the costs in that function are not real.

Understanding Optimization Costs and Penalties:
The cost function blends actual freight charges with penalty costs you invent: a cost per vehicle deployed, a cost per kilometer, a cost per hour, and penalties for early delivery, late delivery and not planning a freight unit at all. None of these invoice anyone. They exist to encode your priorities in a language the algorithm understands.


Figure 1: Planning profile cost settings

Set the non delivery penalty low, and the optimizer will cheerfully leave inconvenient orders behind.
Set earliness and lateness penalties symmetric, and it treats a dock appointment like a suggestion.
Make the per vehicle fixed cost dominant, and it will contort routes to save one truck. This is the part implementation teams underestimate. The optimizer is not a settings screen you configure once; it is a mirror. If your plans come out wrong, the uncomfortable diagnosis is usually that the costs faithfully reflect what you said you value, not what you actually do.

Practical Example:
Freight Consolidation vs Delivery Performance Consider two orders to the same region one 900 kg parcel due Thursday, one 11-tonne load due Friday. A human planner ships them separately: two clean plans, two happy customers, two half-empty trucks. The optimizer, facing a vehicle fixed cost of 500 units against a lateness penalty of 10 per hour, does the arithmetic the planner never writes down. Holding the Thursday order one day and consolidating costs 240 in lateness penalties but saves 500 in vehicle cost. It merges them.

Figure 2: Optimization result with the two Atlanta orders consolidated on one vehicle

Considering Carbon Emissions in Transportation Planning, CO₂ can enter this same calculus. An internal carbon price stops being hypothetical the moment it becomes a cost term the optimizer minimizes alongside distance and duration.

Using VSR Optimization to Improve Transportation Decisions
Run it as a sparring partner, not an autocrat. Interactive planning in the Transportation Cockpit lets planners override the proposal, and the overrides are data. If humans consistently reverse the same category of decision, either train the planners or fix the costs.
Simulate before you commit. Because the cost function is just parameters, counterfactuals are cheap: cut the fleet by two vehicles, tighten delivery windows by four hours, or price carbon at €100 a tonne instead of €50. A profile copy and a re-run replace a consulting engagement.
Let it expose your constraints. Unplanned freight units are the optimizer’s way of filing a complaint. A pattern of unplannable demand on a lane is a procurement insight wearing an error message’s clothing.
Close the loop with execution. Feeding actual transit times back into planning parameters turns every executed freight order into a calibration point.

Conclusion
The SAP TM VSR optimizer demonstrates how transportation planning decisions are influenced not only by freight data and operational constraints but also by the cost parameters and penalties configured by the business. Through the freight consolidation example and practical planning scenarios discussed, we can see how appropriate cost settings, planner judgment, and continuous evaluation of optimization results can improve transportation efficiency and decision making. The key takeaway is that while the optimizer identifies the best solution based on configured objectives, transportation professionals must ensure those objectives reflect actual business priorities.

entry.title: Building an AI Agent Inside SAP CAP — A Developer POC
entry.content:
We have a Fiori app that lists all supplier quotations — extracted from PDFs, stored in CAP, ready to review. The listing part works great. But comparing them? That's where it gets painful. You open one quotation, note the price, go back, open another, try to remember the first one. Do that five times and you're already reaching for Excel.

That's what triggered the idea — the data is all there, the app already has everything, we just needed a smarter way to interact with it.

The interesting thing about @cap-js/agents is that this kind of agent can be built completely standalone as an independent service, or embedded directly inside an existing app. We went with inside the Fiori app — because that's exactly where the quotation data already lives. No duplication, no new backend, no separate deployment.

Two annotations on the CDS service and CAP registers a fully A2A-compliant agent endpoint:

@AGent
@protocol: 'agent'
service QuotationAgentService { ... }

 

The agent gets your OData entities as tools and queries them on demand. But here's the part that made it actually useful — the agent doesn't just return data, it decides how to present it based on the context of the question. Ask "compare total prices across suppliers" and it picks a bar chart because you're comparing across many items with long names. Ask "show quotation status breakdown" and it picks a donut chart because you're looking at proportions of a whole. Ask "how many quotations were submitted over time" and it picks a line chart because that's a trend. The right chart for the right question — automatically.

All of it rendered as SAPUI5 Integration Cards inline in the chat, inside the same Fiori app.

Connected it to Gemini 2.5 Flash via SAP AI Core and built the chat dialog in TypeScript. The hardest part honestly was the prompt — getting the LLM to always pick the right chart type and never skip it took more iterations than the actual code.

entry.title: ABAP to Full Stack: Making Sense of What’s Behind a Fiori App (OData, Class, Virtual Element)
entry.content:
Hello! I’m Andréa Molina. After more than 20 years in SAP, the new SAP world left me completely lost, so I decided to share my experience and learn together. I’m moving from classic ABAP to the SAP full stack, one real project at a time, drama included.

From overwhelmed to curious, my journey had (and still has) a lot of bumps. You can check my other posts here. I hope you find understanding and empathy here, and maybe a few laughs.

If you’re in the same boat, this series is for you. In this post: I will share my experience creating a List Report (a Fiori floorplan) built on a CDS view exposed as OData V4, with a virtual element calculated by an ABAP class. Plus a plot twist in Step 5.

A bit of background

On my journey I always try to use case studies that are real and will add value to the business. The library and ice cream examples just give me more anxiety and make no sense to me. So this time I’m turning an existing query/infoset (SQ01/SQ02) into a Fiori app, to understand how much effort and time it would take.

So far I have worked with the Basic template and one CDS KPI app, and I knew there were more template options to explore. This time I thought the List Report Page would work best (well, not really, but let’s move forward for now... surprise at Step 5 of this blog).

Before we move on, read this if you are asking "What on earth is List Report Page and Basic Template?"
When you create a new app from a template, you can choose among a lot of frameworks. Each framework provides a set of prebuilt files, structure and more.

You can read more about FloorPlans here: https://www.sap.com/design-system/fiori-design-web/v1-136/page-types/floorplans/when-to-use-which-floorplan

The project

Transform an existing Query/InfoSet (SQ01/SQ02) into a Fiori application. 

Does SAP Make This Easy?

In my research and studying I couldn't find a tool that automatically converts queries into Fiori applications. If you know of a better approach, please share it in the comments. I'd genuinely love to learn. 

The Challenge

… because I have never done before this project

  • Create a CDS view that delivers the data exactly the way I want it to be displayed, with logic and not just selection from the database
  • Create an ABAP class that is called by the CDS
  • Understand how the ABAP class and the CDS work together
  • Create a KPI on top of the report list

The best way to learn: get your hands dirty! A simple learning exercise 

I am suggesting here a very simple example of CDS, class and app: create a List Report Page based on a CDS.

The result should show all the Sales Orders created in the last 30 days and flag the ones created today.

Step 0: Eclipse

The way to create backend objects for apps is using the ABAP Development Tools (ADT) in Eclipse. If you are new here, check this tutorial to set up your Eclipse ADT: https://developers.sap.com/tutorials/abap-install-adt/ 

Step 1: The CDS Views

To get familiar with frontend and backend (together, they make the full stack), here is what is what.

  • Backend: where the data comes from.
  • Frontend: the screen the user interacts with. This part of the development is the backend.

What is backend: Where the data comes from. Put in very simple words.  it's the data that will populate the frontend. 

The CDS will select from I_SalesOrder, and we will use a virtual element (calculated by an ABAP class) to flag the orders created today. It will only return the last 30 days, so we don't select hundreds of records. 🥴 

Why I_SalesOrder and not VBAK?

If you grew up in ECC like I did, you might be asking: why not use VBAK?

  • Tables move, CDS adapts. Moving from ECC to S/4HANA changed a lot of tables. Take VBUK, where we used to read the order status. Its fields now live in VBAK, so every program that selected from VBUK needs to change. But a program reading the status through I_SalesOrder will keep working, because SAP updated the view and left the interface alone. That's the idea behind released CDS views: SAP can rearrange it, and your app doesn't notice.
  • Clean core. Clean core is the promise of updating the system faster and more often than before, allowing companies to use the new technologies instead of waiting years for a hard and difficult system upgrade. To do that, you need to use standard objects. If you have already migrated to S/4, you know what I am talking about needing to adapt the system considering all changes. Using CDS views instead of tables is one step in the clean core approach. 
  • It already speaks Fiori. SAP does the hard work of the joins and associations, so you just use it the way you need, and it's all ready for the day you want an Object Page.

Yes, I know. It's not our language YET, we don't know those CDS names yet, and it's so easy to use a table we know. But remember when VBAK sounded just as weird as I_SalesOrder does now? It stuck because we used it every day. This will stick too, if we choose to start.

Now we have AI to help us speed up our knowledge and search for the right object to select from.  But I always use AI as a co-worker and never as the builder and be sure you add on the prompt to use best practices and use Standard objects whenever possible

So let’s go for it! Creating the CDS on Eclipse…

CDS Code 

@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED //Authorization is not required
@EndUserText.label: 'Demo for ABAP Class' //Just a text
@Metadata.ignorePropagatedAnnotations: true //
define view entity ZC_DEMO
 as select from I_SalesOrder
{
     @UI.lineItem:       [{ position: 10, importance: #HIGH }] //The field below will be the first (10) column on the report
     @UI.selectionField: [{ position: 10 }] //The field below will be on the app as a search field
 key SalesOrder,
     @UI.lineItem:       [{ position: 20 }]
     SalesOrderType,
     @UI.lineItem:       [{ position: 30 }]
     SalesOrganization,
     @UI.lineItem:       [{ position: 40 }]
     @UI.selectionField: [{ position: 20 }]
     CreationDate,
     @UI.lineItem:       [{ position: 50, label: 'Created Today' }]
     @ObjectModel.virtualElement: true //The field below will use an virtual Element
     @ObjectModel.virtualElementCalculatedBy: 'ABAP:ZCL_VIRT_DEMO' //This is the Class you use to calculate the field below
     cast( ' ' as abap.char(1) ) as CreatedToday
}
where CreationDate >= dats_add_days( $session.system_date, -30, 'NULL' ) //Just select the last 30 days

UI annotations: how the backend tells the frontend what to draw

The Fiori app doesn’t know anything about our fields. The annotations in the CDS are instructions that travel with the OData service, and Fiori elements reads them to build the screen.

In plain English: the CDS doesn’t only deliver the data, it also sends instructions to the screen the user interacts with: “Hey, look, here is what you show in the table and here is what you show in the filters.” 

 In our code:

  • @UI.lineItem: this field becomes a column in the report.
  • @UI.selectionField: this field becomes a filter in the filter bar at the top.

The position number sets the order: 10 comes first, then 20, and so on.

Note: I prefer using a Metadata Extension (a separate file that keeps the annotations out of the CDS view), but I really want to keep this very simple here.

Step 2: Create the Virtual Class

Note: I know we could get this logic using a CASE in the CDS, but the idea here is to show how to use the class in a very simple example that everybody understand 😉

This part here is important, so let's translate what this part of the code is saying: 

"Hey CDS, this field will use a virtual element. The value will be calculated by an ABAP class called ZCL_VIRT_DEMO. If nothing is returned, the value is blank. The field will contain a value of 1 char (ABAP CHAR1) and will be exposed as CreatedToday. Nice. See you in the class!" 

So now we need to create the virtual class. 

 

The code

CLASS zcl_virt_demo DEFINITION
 PUBLIC                      "Can be used by other objects
 FINAL                       "Cannot be inherited
 CREATE PUBLIC.
 PUBLIC SECTION.
   "This makes the class a calculator for virtual elements
   INTERFACES if_sadl_exit_calc_element_read.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS zcl_virt_demo IMPLEMENTATION.
 "STEP 1 - Runs FIRST, before the database read.
 "Which real fields do you need to calculate your virtual field?"
 METHOD if_sadl_exit_calc_element_read~get_calculation_info.
   "Only if the app really asked for CreatedToday (names come in UPPERCASE)
   IF line_exists( it_requested_calc_elements[ table_line = 'CREATEDTODAY' ] ).
     "Tell SADL to also read CreationDate from the database
     APPEND 'CREATIONDATE' TO et_requested_orig_elements.
   ENDIF.
 ENDMETHOD.
 "STEP 2 - Runs AFTER the database read, once per package of rows.
 "Here we fill the virtual field.
 METHOD if_sadl_exit_calc_element_read~calculate.
   "Table typed with the CDS view, so we can access fields by name
   DATA lt_orders TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zc_demo WITH DEFAULT KEY.
   "Copy the generic data into our typed table
   lt_orders = CORRESPONDING #( it_original_data ).
   "Read the date once, outside the loop (no need to ask on every row)
   DATA(lv_today) = cl_abap_context_info=>get_system_date( ).
   LOOP AT lt_orders ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<order>).
     "Created today? Mark with 'X'
     IF <order>-creationdate = lv_today.
       <order>-createdtoday = 'X'.
     ENDIF.
   ENDLOOP.
   "Give the result back to SADL (same rows, same order)
   ct_calculated_data = CORRESPONDING #( lt_orders ).
 ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

How to debug it

Go to SE24 and search for the class you created. 

Double-click the method you want to debug and create an EXTERNAL breakpoint. 

Important

You can preview the data in Eclipse, right? Yes, but there the class will not be called, and the virtual element comes back blank. Don’t do what I did: I thought my class wasn’t working and spent a long time trying to understand why! Let me save you the trouble: to see the class running, you need to create the service definition, the service binding and the app. 

Step 3: Service Definition and Service Binding

Service Definition - You tell the OData service (the object that selects the data) what you want to be displayed in the result. 

The Code

@EndUserText.label: 'Service Definition for ZC_DEMO'
define service ZUI_DEMO {
 expose ZC_DEMO;
}

Service Binding - You expose the service definition as an OData V4 UI service, so the app can consume your CDS data. 

Activate

When it does not activate

Depending on the architecture of your system, you might not be able to publish your service in Eclipse. If this is your case and you are using V4, you need to go to tcode /n/IWFND/V4_ADMIN. 

Search for your Service Binding, select it and publish it. 

Go back to Eclipse and you will see that the binding is now published.

Step 4: Creating a List Report Page

Just leave the project attributes as they are and finish the project.

You will get a message like the one below:

When it finishes, you will get this message:

  • Open Folder means you will only get this project in BAS.
  • Add Project to Workspace means it will be added to your other projects in BAS. I always use this option. 

Then you can preview the application by right clicking on webapp

The terminal will run and another tab will open with your app! Voilá!

Step 5 - Adding a UI5 element on top of the report

 Until here things went smoothly, but I want to add a Radial Micro Chart on top of the report. So my first instinct was to look for the controller and the view, but there was no MVC… WHAT??????? 

But first, what is MVC?

If you don't know what MVC means and you are an ABAPer, please read this blog post:  Getting cozy with familiar ABAP terms on your new BTP neighborhood 

It was a surprise to me, and then I thought: "Wait... does every template have completely different code and a completely different way of developing?" Gosh! 😅 (Actually, I said a bad word, but let's keep this blog civilized.)

But, as I mentioned in my previous blog Overwhelmed by SAP's new everything? Read this before you give up! I moved from being overwhelmed to being curious, and this time I was curious about how I would add the logic in the backend and not in the frontend.

So I asked Claude and, after a long discussion and a lot of changes, we decided that the best option was to create a Basic app because it was more familiar to me (my first 2 apps were created using Basic Template; be aware that to get to those 2 apps I created like 10 hahahaha).

The main point was that it was very simple to achieve parts of this using the List Report Page, but I couldn't make my UI5 element show up in the app using a custom UI5 extension (a controller file I added to the app), which probably says more about me than about the template. If you know the trick, please tell me. And with the Basic Template, I was trying to reinvent the wheel way too hard.

Then I was like: "There is NO WAY no one wanted to do this before and it is this hard!!"

Trust AI but learn your stuff

I started investigating it. I have taken lots and lots of SAP courses over the course of my career, and many were focused on UX, so I knew about the floorplans. Let's be honest here: it's so easy to think that AI knows more than you do! I think this is going to be the learning curve with this tool: understanding that your expertise matters more than you think.

So I learned that there is something called the Analytical List Page (ALP). The ALP is exactly the combination I was after: KPIs on top, report below. EXACTLY what I need. Claude never suggested it to me until I suggested it to Claude, and then it said that it was obvious that ALP was the best option 😅

What did I learn from this project? 

The nicest thing about being new at something is that once you overcome the first aversion to the new, you learn a lot very fast and mostly by making mistakes. With this project I tried a custom UI5 extension, two new floorplans, an ABAP class in a CDS, an analytical data definition and more.

Now I know when to use an Analytical List Page and when to use a List Report Page. List Report when the goal is to list and filter. ALP when you want KPIs and charts on top, working together with the list below. 

I tried to summarize it all here so you could learn from my experience. Let me know if it worked! 😉

——————

While this post might be basic to some, I added here everything that was getting me overwhelmed for years and all my questions related to those things. My goal with these posts is to demystify the new SAP development world together with you.

I'll continue sharing simple posts based on real discoveries, real questions and real experiences, sharing my journey, my learnings and my bumps along the way so you don't need to go through some of them yourself.

If you're in the same boat, stay tuned. There will be many more posts about this journey.

If you're further along than this, pretty please help us in the comments.

To be continued

I’m on holiday now, in Brazil to be more exact , so there’s no ALP update yet (yes, I’m still writing here, apparently I can’t help it 😅). But I will write about the Analytical List Page as soon as I’m back and get it sorted. And I promise to tell you honestly what worked and what didn’t. 

Thanks for reading!

entry.title: UI5 TypeScript development just got smoother
entry.content:
No more @namespace annotations: ui5-tooling-transpile now auto-detects your UI5 namespace

If you write UI5 with TypeScript, you have almost certainly written this in every controller, control, and component:

/**
 * @namespace ui5.ecosystem.demo.myapp
 */
export default class Main extends Controller {

That annotation exists for one reason: the Babel preset that converts your TypeScript class to a classic sap.ui.define call needs to know which namespace prefix to put in front of controller.Main. Without it, the generated module name comes out wrong and the app breaks at runtime.

Starting with ui5-tooling-transpile 3.14.0, you do not need to write it anymore.

What changed

The new version of babel-preset-transform-ui5 (7.11.0) can derive the namespace from the project structure on its own. ui5-tooling-transpile now reads the namespace and source path configuration from your ui5.yaml, builds the sourceFolders map (a table that says "files under webapp/ belong to this namespace"), and hands it directly to the preset before transpilation starts.

The result is that every file in your project picks up the right namespace prefix automatically. You delete the annotations, and the output is identical to what you had before.

Here is what a controller looks like before and after:

// before
/**
 * @namespace ui5.ecosystem.demo.myapp
 */
export default class Main extends Controller {
  onInit(): void {
    // ...
  }
}
// after
export default class Main extends Controller {
  onInit(): void {
    // ...
  }
}

Same output. One annotation fewer per file. In a medium-sized app with a dozen controllers and a handful of controls, that is a meaningful amount of noise gone.

What it covers

The auto-detection works across all three scenarios you are likely to encounter.

App development. The middleware and the build task both read the project's namespace from ui5.yaml. Files under webapp/ (or whatever path you have configured in resources.configuration.paths.webapp) map to that namespace. Nothing to configure.

Library development. For library projects src/ maps to the project namespace. Same automatic derivation, same zero-config experience.

Middleware with a dependency library. This is the case that was missing before and is the main reason the change landed. When your app runs ui5 serve with ui5-tooling-transpile as middleware, and one of your workspace library dependencies also uses ui5-tooling-transpile, the middleware now walks the dependency graph and registers the sourceFolders of each dependency alongside your own. So if a controller from a local library gets served through the middleware, it resolves to my.lib.controller.Shared instead of src.controller.Shared. No annotations needed in the library either.

External Babel configs. If your project supplies a .babelrc, babel.config.js, or similar, the auto-derived sourceFolders is normally not injected because the external config takes over. Add injectSourceFolders: true to your ui5.yaml configuration block for ui5-tooling-transpile and the preset will receive the derived values, with anything already set in your external config taking precedence:

builder:
  customTasks:
    - name: ui5-tooling-transpile-task
      afterTask: replaceVersion
      configuration:
        injectSourceFolders: true

How to upgrade

Update ui5-tooling-transpile to 3.14.0 or later in your project:

npm install ui5-tooling-transpile@latest --save-dev

Then delete the @namespace JSDoc blocks from your TypeScript source files. That's it. If you use an external Babel config and want to stop writing annotations there too, add injectSourceFolders: true as shown above.

The Easy UI5 TypeScript templates have been updated to match, so new projects generated from those templates will start without annotations from the beginning.

Where to find it

The package is on npm:

👉 https://www.npmjs.com/package/ui5-tooling-transpile

It's part of the ui5-ecosystem-showcase, the collection of UI5 CLI extensions the community uses every day. The showcase itself runs without any @namespace annotations now, so the complete set of app and library scenarios there serves as a working reference.
